judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Stiff, slightly bureaucratic exposition ('there's another task which I need performed', 'requested he create'), odd possessive [Person]', and a terse shouted reminder; the turn to an off-screen death folded into the thanks is very Westwood.

items.label: B
items.critique: Short, breathless, a little awkward ('That evil one defeated both of my novices'), with a capitalised 'the Necromancer' in the journal; the reward is a hand-off to the next quest, not a gift speech.

items.label: C
items.critique: Tidy template: greeting, problem, a lost farmhand for colour, a question with a direction and a meeting place, then a gift and a 'stock up at the shops first' hint; too orderly and too signposted for Westwood.

items.label: D
items.critique: Clumsy-real lines ('he'll be destroyed', 'Could you... would you get it back for us?') and a thin one-line thanks; the journal names 'an Ogre near the docks' slightly off from the offer, a typical Westwood unevenness.

items.label: E
items.critique: Ornate, pseudo-archaic register ('sorely need', 'turn the [Thing] to the foulest of ends, for certain!', 'more useful than you know') and stacked clauses; 'Wanderer' as address and the overwrought reminder read as pastiche.

items.label: F
items.critique: Plain and Nox-like in length, but the 'At last!' opener with no context, the neat key handoff and the forge pointer read as a designed quest beat; reminder 'Take heart, one puny Imp can't do much harm' is a writer's wink.

items.label: G
items.critique: Character-comedy self-introduction ('I am Master [Person]', 'half-blind old man', 'Hmmm... Quite so.') and a three-page thanks that sets up lessons; more personality-sketch than Westwood's flat functional voice.

items.label: H
items.critique: Melodramatic setup ('a raving demoness', wife turned into a wolf) with run-on comma splices and an impatient reminder; effusive 'brave and kind Adventurer' thanks and the odd [Person]' possessive fit Westwood.

tells: Westwood's texts are a little clumsy: comma splices, odd possessives, journal lines that do not quite match the offer, stiff phrasing ('a task which I need performed'); the new texts are cleaner and more evenly built.

New texts follow a visible template (greeting, problem, colourful aside, question with direction, reward plus a pointer to the next NPC or the shops); Westwood often skips steps or makes the thanks a bare one-liner.
New texts give speakers comic personality flourishes (self-introductions, 'Hmmm... Quite so', winking reminders); Westwood's NPCs are flatter and more urgent.
Pseudo-archaic ornament ('sorely', 'foulest of ends', 'for certain', 'more useful than you know') marks pastiche rather than Westwood's plain register.
Several new texts reuse the same monster (Imps) and the same 'little devils' phrasing; repeated stock creatures and words across a packet point to one generator.
